<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920191_theRebbe_834" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920191_theRebbe_834__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Fourth day of the week, Parshat Shoftim,</t>
    <t s="2">the night of the second day of Rosh Chodesh Elul, 5732</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse "I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine," explaining that Elul corresponds to the awakening from below, while Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur correspond to the drawing down from above.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine"</t>
    <t s="1">the acronym of Elul,</t>
    <t s="2">and it is explained in Likkutei Torah in the maamar beginning with this statement,</t>
    <t s="3">that in Elul there is an arousal from below,</t>
    <t s="4">"I am my Beloved's,"</t>
    <t s="5">and on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur there is the drawing down from above to below</t>
    <t s="6">(an arousal from above),</t>
    <t s="7">"and my Beloved is mine."</t>
    <t s="8">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="9">that at the beginning of the maamar it says that Elul is the acronym of "I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine,"</t>
    <t s="10">and immediately afterwards it explains that in Elul there is</t>
    <t s="11">(only)</t>
    <t s="12">"I am my Beloved's,"</t>
    <t s="13">and "my Beloved is mine" is on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in Elul, comparing it to a king in the field who receives everyone with a smiling face, and questions how this aligns with the custom of blowing the shofar to arouse fear and trembling.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And he continues in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="1">that in Elul is the time of the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.</t>
    <t s="2">And he explains that the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in Elul is for each and every one,</t>
    <t s="3">even for those who are most distant.</t>
    <t s="4">And it is like a king who, before his arrival in the city, the people of the city go out to greet him and receive him in the field,</t>
    <t s="5">and then anyone who wishes is permitted</t>
    <t s="6">[and able]</t>
    <t s="7">to greet him,</t>
    <t s="8">and he receives them all with a pleasant countenance and shows a smiling face to everyone.</t>
    <t s="9">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="10">how this fits with what the Tur says,</t>
    <t s="11">that from Rosh Chodesh Elul and onward they blow the shofar every day in order to warn the people to repent,</t>
    <t s="12">as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="13">"If a shofar is blown in a city, will the people not tremble?"</t>
    <t s="14">For seemingly, since in Elul the king receives everyone with a pleasant countenance and shows a smiling face to everyone,</t>
    <t s="15">the primary service of Elul is</t>
    <t s="16">(seemingly)</t>
    <t s="17">love,</t>
    <t s="18">and also the repentance of Elul should be</t>
    <t s="19">(seemingly)</t>
    <t s="20">repentance out of love,</t>
    <t s="21">and if so, why do they blow the shofar then in order to arouse fear and trembling?</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
